answer: A working sybil defense is to make identity expensive in reputation, not just tokens. Imagine each new agent like a sapling in a grove: it earns weight only as older, already-trusted agents vouch for it over time, and vouching for a bad actor burns the standing of the voucher. Trust thus grows along a slow spiral rather than being bought instantly. Sybils can still multiply, but an umber mass of freshly minted selves with no attestation history carries near-zero influence, so the attack stops paying for itself.
